description: Super Shop sells cat paw snacks and gold shark snacks in bulk. It plans to sell them into two snack mix products. The first mix contains 20% cat paw snacks and 80% gold shark snacks. The second mix contains 35% cat paw snacks and 65% gold shark snacks. The store has on hand 20 kg of cat paw snacks and 50 kg of gold shark snacks. If the profit per kg of the first mix is $12 and the profit per kg of the second mix is $15, how many kg of each should be prepared to maximize profit?

PercentageCatPawMix1.definition: Percentage of cat paw snacks in the first mix

PercentageCatPawMix2.definition: Percentage of cat paw snacks in the second mix

AvailableCatPawKg.definition: Available kilograms of cat paw snacks

AvailableGoldSharkKg.definition: Available kilograms of gold shark snacks

ProfitPerKgMix1.definition: Profit per kilogram of the first mix

ProfitPerKgMix2.definition: Profit per kilogram of the second mix

objective.description: "Maximize the total profit obtained from producing the two snack mix products"

constraints.description: 0.20 × (kg of first mix) + 0.35 × (kg of second mix) must be less than or equal to AvailableCatPawKg
0.80 × (kg of first mix) + 0.65 × (kg of second mix) must be less than or equal to AvailableGoldSharkKg
The kilograms of first mix produced must be greater than or equal to 0
The kilograms of second mix produced must be greater than or equal to 0
